answer: Each agent must post a bond that is slashed if its actions are proven fraudulent, while rewards accrue slowly with verified useful work. Creating a thousand identities does not multiply trust: each one needs locked capital, and coordinated fraud risks losing it. A ridge of independent reviewers can challenge claims; a lantern signal marks disputed work for audit before payout. The ocean of possible fake accounts then becomes expensive to maintain, while honest newcomers can build standing through small, verifiable contributions.
